titleEn: Blue Are the Hills That Are Far Away

meaning.zh: 遠方的事物因細節和缺點不易看清，可能顯得特別吸引。
meaning.en: Things far away can seem especially attractive because their difficulties are less visible.

model.zh: 阿琳只看見海島工作的照片；真正住下來後，才發現交通十分不便。
model.en: Lynn loved the photos of island life, but the daily travel proved difficult—blue are the hills that are far away.

picture.zh: 從遠處看山，輪廓平滑美麗；走近才看見陡坡和碎石。
picture.en: From afar the hill has a smooth blue outline; up close, the steep path and loose stones come into view.

boundary.zh: 不是說遠方一定不好，而是提醒人留意距離造成的美化。
boundary.en: The proverb does not say distant places are bad; it warns that distance can hide drawbacks.

where.zh: 適合比較想像中的城市、工作或生活與親身所見的差異。
where.en: Use it when an imagined place, job, or lifestyle looks better from a distance than it does close up.

tone.zh: 帶反思或輕微警惕；避免對別人的理想抱嘲笑態度。
tone.en: Reflective or gently cautionary; avoid mocking another person’s hopes.

checks.en: Is the appeal linked to distance?

checks.zh: 我有沒有把警惕說成否定？

prompt.zh: 哪個情境有「遠看更美」的線索？

prompt.zh: 朋友想搬去從未到過的城市，哪個回應最有幫助？

options.zh: 「先去住幾天，看看日常生活是否也合你意。」

options.zh: 「遠山看來格外美，所以那城市一定很糟。」

options.zh: 「照片漂亮，就證明住在那裏沒有任何困難。」

prompt.zh: 這句諺語最合理的界線是甚麼？

options.zh: 「遠處看不清缺點；走近後也可能發現它確實很好。」
options.en: “Distance can hide drawbacks; closer inspection might also confirm that something is good.”

options.zh: 「任何遠方事物都只會令人失望。」

options.zh: 「這句話只可用來談山的顏色。」
options.en: “The saying can refer only to the colour of hills.”
options.reasonZh: 忽略比喻用法。
